candidate.answerReason: The angle conditions allow arithmetic progressions with spacing 20 or 30 degrees. The latter is attainable and gives largest angles 105 and 135 degrees, totaling 240 degrees.

methods.label: Use supplementary pairs and the middle triangle angle
methods.explanation:
Measure all angles in degrees. First order the quadrilateral's four angles from smallest to largest. Since their sum is \(360\), an arithmetic progression of four angles can be written as
\[
90-3t,\quad 90-t,\quad 90+t,\quad 90+3t,
\]
where \(0\le t<30\). This range follows from positivity of the smallest angle. In particular, every angle is less than \(180\), so the quadrilateral is convex and diagonal \(BD\) divides its angles at \(B\) and \(D\).

Let the angles of triangle \(ABD\) at \(A,B,D\) be \(x,y,z\), respectively. Then \(x+y+z=180\). The stated correspondence gives the angles of triangle \(DCB\) at \(D,C,B\) as \(x,y,z\). Consequently, the quadrilateral angles at \(A,B,C,D\) are
\[
x,\quad y+z=180-x,\quad y,\quad x+z=180-y.
\]
Thus they occur in supplementary pairs. The case \(t=0\) would give \(x=y=90\) and \(z=0\), which is impossible, so \(0<t<30\).

The supplementary pairs in the ordered progression are
\[
\{90-3t,90+3t\},\qquad
\{90-t,90+t\}.
\]
The angles \(x\) and \(y\) must come from different pairs, since choosing a supplementary pair would force \(z=0\). Also, \(x+y<180\). These restrictions leave exactly two possibilities, allowing \(x\) and \(y\) to exchange roles:
\[
\{x,y,z\}=\{90-3t,90-t,4t\}
\]
or
\[
\{x,y,z\}=\{90-3t,90+t,2t\}.
\]
A triangle whose angles form an arithmetic progression has middle angle \(60\), because its three angles sum to \(180\). In the first possibility, setting one of the three expressions equal to \(60\) gives \(t=10,30,15\); only \(10\) and \(15\) lie in \((0,30)\). In the second possibility, the candidates are \(t=10,-30,30\), leaving only \(10\). Therefore every allowed quadrilateral has \(t\le15\).

Its two largest angles have sum
\[
(90+t)+(90+3t)=180+4t\le240.
\]
To attain this bound, take triangle \(ABD\) with angles \(45,75,60\) at \(A,B,D\), and construct triangle \(DCB\) on the other side of \(BD\) with angles \(45,75,60\) at \(D,C,B\). The resulting quadrilateral has angles \(45,135,75,105\), whose ordered values are \(45,75,105,135\). All conditions hold, and the two largest total \(\boxed{240}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).

candidate.annotationRationale: The targets are the arithmetic-progression constraints and the corresponding-angle relationships in similar triangles. Triangle and quadrilateral angle sums produce supplementary pairs, while the arithmetic-middle property identifies the triangle's 60-degree angle. No side-ratio calculation or general sequence formula is required.
